airvault-offlineNote: Offline Mode blocks blockchain requests. A physical air gap requires an isolated computer.

airvault-emptyHistory: Signing and verification activity will appear here.

airvault-step2Help: Transfer the .avreq to the signer. Check every input, output and fee.
airvault-step3Help: Return the .avsig to the connected computer for verification and broadcast.
airvault-entropyHelp: A word encodes 11 bits. The final word includes checksum bits. Prefix bits are preserved; the OS supplies the remainder. Memorable words are not random.
airvault-rawHelp: Enter exactly 128 or 256 unbiased binary digits from your independently verified entropy process.
airvault-keyPasswordHelp: Protects this root and its identities. Leave empty to use vault protection. Account labels do not create independent encryption.
airvault-ceremonyHelp: Write every word in order. You have five minutes to hide and re-enter the phrase. Back up BIP39 passphrases separately. This phrase will not be shown again after confirmation.
airvault-hidePhrase: I recorded it — hide and verify
airvault-passphraseHelp: Arbitrary text that creates a different wallet. Losing it makes its accounts unrecoverable even with the recovery phrase.
airvault-pathHelp: Changing the path changes the address. Initial transaction signing supports BIP84 / native SegWit.
airvault-exportPrivacy: Public bundles reveal addresses and wallet relationships. Keep them private.
airvault-utxoHelp: Provide full previous transactions and output indices. Provider state is external and may be stale.
airvault-reviewHelp: Amounts and addresses are decoded from the PSBT. Supplied descriptions are untrusted context.
airvault-approveCheck: I verified the network, every recipient, the amounts, and the fee.
airvault-signHelp: Review approval expires after two minutes and is single-use.
airvault-broadcastCheck: I reviewed the signed transaction and authorize broadcasting it.
airvault-backupHelp: Includes encrypted secrets and metadata. Restore requires the vault password and custom root passwords for their protected keys.
airvault-backupCheck: I authorize creating this encrypted secret-bearing backup.
airvault-restoreHelp: Restore on a fresh profile. Existing vaults are never overwritten. Dry run checks authentication and metadata integrity.
airvault-restoreDone: Restored. Enter the backup's vault password to unlock.
airvault-settingsConfirm: I confirm these security and mode changes.
airvault-providerHelp: Use an Esplora endpoint for your chosen network. AirVault checks its genesis block. HTTPS required, except localhost. Offline Mode never uses it.
airvault-mcpDisabled: Not included in this Windows preview. The planned integration will not be allowed to unlock, sign, or export secrets.
airvault-supportHelp: This Windows preview enables Bitcoin native SegWit signing. Other operations remain unavailable until their adapters and verification tests are complete.
airvault-savedRequest: Request prepared. Review before export or signing.
airvault-requiredPrefix: Enter exactly the selected number of manual words.
airvault-bytesInfo: Transfer files using USB or your separate QR Transceiver.
airvault-guideTitle: How to verify your dice-generated BIP39 words manually
airvault-diceBasic: Roll a physical six-sided die. Enter the number you rolled below. Rolls 1, 2, or 3 become 0; rolls 4, 5, or 6 become 1. After 11 rolls, check the result and add the word to your prefix.
airvault-fairDice: Use a fair physical die and independent rolls. Do not invent a pattern or repeatedly click a number. This mapping is unbiased only when the two groups are equally likely.
airvault-generatorBasic: Name your wallet, choose a phrase length and entropy method, and record your prefix words. The default is 11 dice-generated words plus operating-system randomness for a 24-word phrase. Review each word, generate the full phrase, write it down privately, then hide and re-enter it to finish.
airvault-fullDiceHelp: Each die roll supplies one entropy bit. Enter 256 rolls for a 24-word phrase, or 128 for a 12-word phrase. AirVault then computes the checksum. Do not roll an independent final word.
airvault-invalidRoll: Enter a whole die value from 1 to 6.
airvault-tooManyRolls: This group is complete. Undo or reset before entering another roll.
airvault-elevenRolls: Exactly 11 rolls are required for one word.
airvault-invalidWord: Enter one word from the BIP39 English list.
airvault-checkboxHelp: This checkbox records your own check. It is not cryptographic proof of independent verification.
airvault-independentList: Check against an independently obtained copy of the official wordlist when possible. A list bundled in the same app cannot independently establish that the app itself is trustworthy.
airvault-findWord: Find a word or printed position
airvault-publicExample: Public example — never use this as wallet entropy
airvault-manualSteps:
1. Roll an ordinary six-sided die 11 times.
2. Write down each result in the order rolled.
3. Convert each roll: 1, 2, 3 become 0; 4, 5, 6 become 1.
4. Write the 11 binary digits in the same order.
5. Assign these weights, from left to right:
   1024 512 256 128 64 32 16 8 4 2 1
6. Add the weights whose bit is 1. Ignore weights whose bit is 0.
7. The total is the word's zero-based index (0–2047).
8. Add 1 for a printed list numbered 1–2048.
9. Find that position in the official BIP39 English wordlist.
10. Compare its word with AirVault's result.

If they match, you have independently checked the dice-to-word mapping.
airvault-advancedEntropy: BIP39 encodes ENT + ENT/32 bits in 11-bit word indices. A 24-word phrase has 256 entropy bits and 8 checksum bits; a 12-word phrase has 128 entropy bits and 4 checksum bits. SHA-256 of the entropy supplies the leading checksum bits. The final word contains entropy and checksum bits, so it cannot be chosen as an independent word.
airvault-advancedPrefix: Prefix words preserve their full 11-bit indices, including leading zeroes. The default 11-word prefix uses 121 of 256 bits; the OS CSPRNG fills the remaining 135 bits before the checksum is appended. Up to 23 prefix words are allowed for 24 words, or 11 for 12 words. Human-chosen words may have much less entropy than random dice rolls.
airvault-secretWorksheet: Your actual rolls and word calculations remain available only during this creation ceremony. They are cleared when you finish, cancel, leave the page, or lock. They are never logged, persisted, exported, or exposed through MCP. JavaScript and operating-system memory cannot be guaranteed to erase every historical copy.
airvault-basicVault:
1. Choose Offline signer for the machine holding recovery phrases. Use Proxy for a separate watch-only machine, or Combined for disposable testing on one machine.
2. Create a vault with a unique password of at least 12 characters.
3. Open Wallets to generate or import a test phrase. Write a newly generated phrase down before hiding it; AirVault will ask you to re-enter it.
4. Open Accounts and derive a native SegWit account (BIP84). Choose the intended Bitcoin network explicitly.
5. Export public accounts (.avpub) to the proxy. The proxy can view addresses without recovery phrases.
6. Prepare a transfer on the proxy, export its request (.avreq), and import it on the signer.
7. Review all decoded destinations, amounts, inputs and fees. Approve signing locally and export .avsig.
8. Import .avsig on the proxy, review the verified transaction, and explicitly approve broadcast.
airvault-advancedVault: This preview signs single-key Bitcoin native SegWit (P2WPKH, SIGHASH_ALL) transactions. BIP44, BIP49 and BIP86 address derivation is available, but their signing paths are not enabled. Every input must include its complete previous transaction. Unknown scripts, unsupported sighashes and partially signed requests are rejected. Network and context fields are bound into the request digest; recipients and fees are independently decoded from the PSBT.
airvault-advancedProvider: Network access is available only in Proxy or Combined mode and only after an explicit action. Configure an Esplora-compatible URL for the selected chain. HTTPS is required except for loopback development services. Use separate vault profiles for signer and proxy. The offline-only executable removes the provider dependency at compile time.
airvault-basicBackup: Create an encrypted backup in Settings and test restoring it into a new profile. Keep the vault password, optional custom root passwords and BIP39 passphrases available separately. A forgotten BIP39 passphrase cannot be recovered from the mnemonic; each passphrase derives a different wallet.
airvault-helpOffline: All instructions, the public example and the wordlist below work offline. Open the official link in a separate online browser. Never paste actual recovery words into a website.
